title: A Crown for the Spire
premise: Oscar Oyelaran, runaway apprentice to a hedge-witch, has spent three years hiding in the Ledgerhouse of the Guild of Impossible Things, keeping accounts of traded souls, borrowed years, and bottled luck. When the border wards collapse and the stars go out on the same night, Oscar discovers his own name in a ledger entry he never made: sold, decades ago, to the court beneath the mountain. To survive the long winter falling over the world and reclaim what was taken from him, he must descend into that court, out-bargain its hungry king, and steal back not only his soul but those of everyone the ledgers ever bound. He succeeds at terrible cost — the guild's mistress pays with her own name, and Oscar, soul restored but no longer able to lie, becomes the new keeper of an honest ledger.
about_author: F. M. Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three collections of books that technically did not exist. They write fantasy about paperwork, bargains, and the people who fall through the cracks between both.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. During a routine audit of impossible inventory, the border wards shatter and every star vanishes at once; in the panic, Oscar finds his own name inked in a ledger dated before his birth. The beat is dread disguised as competence — a man who trusts numbers discovering the numbers were lying about him.

chapters.title: An Inventory of Stolen Souls
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Interrogating the guild's mistress, Vess Corvane, he learns the trade: souls sold beneath the mountain buy the guild's immunity from winter. She admits she signed his name as collateral long ago. The emotional beat is betrayal curdling into resolve — Oscar chooses to go down rather than be spent.

chapters.title: What the Hedge-Witch Knew
chapters.summary: Flashback chapters braided with present travel: young Oscar flees his master, Mother Ilse, after reading her true grimoire — she was the one who first sold his soul to save him from a fever. POV alternates Oscar and Ilse. The beat is grief: his origin story is a debt he never agreed to.

chapters.title: The Road Where Winter Began
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, joined by Sable, a disgraced ward-smith whose failed wards caused the collapse. Villages they pass are freezing mid-sentence, time pooling like ice. The beat is reluctant partnership — two people responsible for catastrophe learning to carry it together instead of alone.

chapters.title: A Bargain at the Tollbridge
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A toll-keeper demands payment in memories; Sable trades her memory of why she built the wards wrong, and Oscar realizes she may have been coerced by the court itself. The beat is suspicion giving way to protectiveness — Oscar lies for the first time to shield her, and hates how easily it comes.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Descent through a cavern city lit by caged starlight — the missing stars. The court's king, patient and courteous, greets Oscar as 'the account come due.' The beat is seduction: the king offers Oscar comfort, permanence, a place where nothing is owed, and part of him wants to accept.

chapters.title: Ledgers of the Hungry King
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Allowed access to the court's archives, he discovers the king's secret: the court is starving because it bought more souls than any world can hold, and the long winter is digestion. The beat is horrified clarity — the corruption of power shown as bookkeeping, and Oscar sees himself in it.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The king offers each of them escape at another's expense; Sable nearly takes it, then burns her last ward-craft to break the cages holding the stolen stars. The beat is sacrifice — survival redefined as what you refuse to buy. The court begins to crack around them.

chapters.title: The Audit of Heaven
chapters.summary: Climax, Oscar's POV. Before the fleeing court, Oscar invokes guild law: every contract audited, every soul returned, debts settled against the king's own hoard. Vess arrives to co-sign, paying with her name — she becomes unremembered by all. The beat is triumph laced with mourning; justice achieved outside any law but the one they write together.

chapters.title: A Crown for the Spire
chapters.summary: Resolution, Oscar's POV. Stars return; winter breaks. Offered the guild's leadership, Oscar instead founds a public ledger where every bargain is written honestly, taking Mother Ilse in as its first witness. The beat is quiet restoration — power accepted only as stewardship, and a keeper who can no longer lie keeping faith with the world.
